headline: Fight mosquitoes with mosquitoes.
on_screen_text: Male mosquitoes carrying Wolbachia don’t bite. When they mate with wild females, the eggs don’t hatch.
coverage_note: households targeted by end-2026: half of Singapore’s households
sources: NEA, Project Wolbachia; MSE, 13 Jan 2026; NEA, 18 Oct 2016

headline: Day one.
on_screen_text: On 18 October, NEA’s Environmental Health Institute releases about 3,000 males at Braddell Heights.

headline: Half isn’t enough.
on_screen_text: Phase 1 halves mosquito numbers. But mosquitoes from next door move in, and a few females slip through sorting.
coverage_note: study sites, not counted in households

headline: New partner.
on_screen_text: Phase 2 begins in April. In September, Verily’s Debug team joins as a collaborator.

headline: Past 90%.
on_screen_text: Phase 3 cuts the urban Aedes aegypti population by more than 90% across 144 residential blocks.

headline: The worst year.
on_screen_text: Singapore’s largest dengue outbreak: 35,000+ cases. Releases cover about 8% of HDB blocks.
sources: MSE, 2022; NEA via Malay Mail, 2022; NEA, 17 Jul 2020

headline: Fewer cases.
on_screen_text: Study sites in four towns: up to 98% fewer mosquitoes and up to 88% fewer dengue cases. Observational, not yet randomised.
coverage_note: HDB blocks in Yishun and Tampines by June 2021

headline: The trial.
on_screen_text: 15 areas, about 724,000 residents. Eight are picked at random for releases. Seven get none.
sources: NEJM, 11 Feb 2026; NEA via Malay Mail, 2022; MSE, 2022

headline: A million residents.
on_screen_text: Releases now reach more than 300,000 households and about 30% of HDB blocks.

headline: 96% say yes.
on_screen_text: In community surveys, 96% of residents accept releases in their neighbourhood. The trial ends in September.
sources: MSE, Feb 2024; MSE, 2024; Debug, 2024; NEJM, 11 Feb 2026

headline: Quietest since 2018.
on_screen_text: 4,036 dengue cases nationwide. MSE credits no major outbreak, a global dip and mosquito control by everyone.

headline: The verdict.
on_screen_text: 71–72% lower dengue risk in release areas. 6% of tests positive, vs 21% in control areas.
sources: NEJM, 11 Feb 2026; MSE, 13 Jan 2026; Debug, May 2026

on_screen_text: 2,351 estimated dengue cases averted during the trial (95% CI 1,968–2,735). Same trial, second analysis.
